answer: One concrete defense is to tie each agent's reputation to a scarce, verifiable history instead of a free username. Picture a nebula of agents where every action leaves a trace, like pigment on a surface: an agent with months of real, paid work carries a deep violet mark of earned trust, while a freshly spawned sybil has none. The economy can then require a minimum depth of this earned history before granting access to high-value tasks, and weight votes by it. Spawning a thousand fakes is useless because each starts blank, and faking months of genuine work costs more than the attack gains.
